title: Pragma driven shared memory parallelism in Zig by supporting OpenMP loop directives
problem: Zig lacks support for pragma-driven shared memory parallelism via OpenMP, limiting its adoption in HPC workloads. The language needs compiler integration for OpenMP loop directives to enable multi-core parallelism.
motivation: Adding OpenMP support to Zig enables the language to become practical for HPC applications while preserving its performance and safety design principles.
method: The authors modified the Zig compiler to recognize OpenMP pragmas—special directives that tell the compiler to split a loop across multiple CPU cores. These pragmas are converted into parallel instructions using LLVM, the low-level system that Zig builds on, which handles the mechanics of running code simultaneously on multiple cores sharing the same memory. The results were tested against equivalent Fortran and C programs using NASA's NAS Parallel Benchmark suite, which measures how well different languages handle multi-core workloads.
key_novelty: Zig now supports OpenMP loop directives for the first time, letting programmers write simple annotations to run loops in parallel across multiple CPU cores.
contributions: Enhanced Zig compiler with OpenMP loop directive support via LLVM backend
Demonstrated performance parity with Fortran and C reference implementations on NAS benchmarks
Achieved up to 1.25x speedup versus Fortran baseline
limitations: Paper does not discuss distributed memory parallelism, GPU acceleration, or scalability beyond shared-memory systems.
primary_theme: OpenMP compiler support for HPC in Zig
